column1: # EXP-R2-243 RITA-xl context-information qualification, re-measured under the
# checkpoint's native document rendering, with the pre-repair rendering beside it.
# WHY THIS RUN EXISTS. RITA-xl was declared `input_format="raw"`: a bare residue
# string, which the released post-processor renders as `seq<EOS>` because its
# template is Sequence-then-`<EOS>` and prefixes nothing. The checkpoint's
# training stream is documents separated by that token, so a document is preceded
# by one, and the arm was scored with no boundary for its first residue to be
# conditioned on. `input_format` is now `eos_bounded_seq` -- the declared
# document boundary, then the sequence, with the tokenizer's terminal `<EOS>`
# still appended -- and nothing else about the estimand, the cohort, the
# reference, the dtype, the seed or the bootstrap changed. Before this campaign
# the format effect was measured directly on the checkpoint: over the gate's own
# draw (200 Swiss-Prot records of 64-246 residues, seed 20260728, float32), at
# the position after one `<EOS>` the model places 0.99963 of its next-token mass
# on the 20 residue ids (mean over 64 records) and assigns the first residue a
# mean NLL of 0.7973 +/- 0.0333 nats; over the tokens both renderings score --
# residues 2..L and the terminal `<EOS>` -- the boundary-prefixed rendering costs
# 1.24520 nats/token against the bare rendering's 1.40124, a paired per-record
# mean difference of -0.17384 +/- 0.01383 nats/token over 200 records, against
# -0.00618 for a `<PAD>`-prefixed control.
# WHAT MOVED BESIDES THE RENDERING, stated rather than left to be inferred. The
# rendering declares one marker id: the boundary it prefixes, which is the same
# id the tokenizer appends as its terminator, so an exclusion stated by id
# removes both. The scored targets are therefore the sequence's residues, 1..L,
# where the bare rendering scored residues 2..L plus that terminator. The scored
# *count* per record is L either way and the scored *positions* are unchanged
# (input indices 1..L); the *membership* changes by one token per record,
# residue 1's term entering and the terminator's leaving. That is the span this
# arm's own declaration states, not a second convention: it is the statement
# `rendering_marker_ids` makes for this format and the one
# `budget.scored_tokens` applies to every other arm. EXP-R2-242's sibling repair
# for ProGen3 moved that lineage's span to its residues for the same reason.
# WHY THERE ARE TWO KEYS. `native` is the repaired code (this campaign's commit)
# and `base` is the pre-repair code, frozen at the commit this campaign's commit
# is built on. They differ in the rendering and in the span resolution and in
# nothing else, so the pair is a measured statement of what the repair moved on
# the same pod, the same draw and the same sidecar design -- and `base` is also a
# same-day reproduction of the recorded 8-block envelope, which is a diagnostic of
# the record rather than a replacement for it. This is a new measurement, not a
# correction of the old one: new run-id, new artefacts and the recorded envelopes
# are left exactly as they are. A FAIL or an interval containing zero is a
# completed measurement and is reported as one.
# The draw is the eight frozen EXP-R2-216/224/240 blocks, unchanged: pool 4000,
# --cohort-draw-seed 20260728, --cohort-skip 7000k for k = 0..7, band 64-246,
# n 200, held-out unigram reference 4000, --seed 20260727, disjoint estimator.
# Cohort.digest hashes records only and the records are the same ones, so each
# cell's expect basename carries that block's existing digest: a cell that drew
# anything else writes a differently named file and is reported no-artifact
# rather than silently paired against a block it does not share. All sixteen
# stage-01 cells are expected to carry the eight recorded digests, in order.
# --allow-second-stage-arms is this campaign's door and admits only
# STAGED_SECOND_STAGE_ARMS. float32 and --skip-truncation as before: rita-xl's
# native encoding does not go through tokenize_batch, and a bfloat16 reading of
# this checkpoint is a different measurement (its remote attention mixes float32
# and half). --batch-size 1 as before: the encoding assigns no pad token and the
# forward takes no attention mask, so records are scored one at a time. The
# rendering adds one token per record; the longest record in the band is 246
# residues, so 248 tokens, and the 1024-position context is not reached.
# Stage 41 runs over one key's eight sidecars alone at its recorded settings
# (seed 20260820, 2000 paired bootstrap, --alpha-sweep 1.0), as a `cpu` row so
# that it holds no card. Identification is the displacement-corrected lower bound
# above zero on all eight blocks, and both keys are read the same way.
# gpu and slot: this campaign shares the pod with another agent's running
# ProGen3 campaign, so it holds the two cards that were idle when it was written
# (cuda:2 and cuda:3) and takes one slot per pair of blocks. TRANSFER_PYTHON is
# the same GPFS ct runtime the recorded cells ran under, so the two runs differ
# in the code under test and not in the interpreter.
